caption: A cold metal railing on a humid summer morning is covered in fine droplets, and a finger drags through them leaving a clear line.

sa.check: A metal railing is covered in fine droplets.
A finger drags through the droplets.
A clear line is left where the finger passed.
The droplets around the line stay in place.
The drag comes first and the line follows.

pc.expect: The line is clear where the finger wiped and the droplets away from it stay in place.
pc.fail: The droplets vanish from the untouched parts of the railing as the line is drawn; or droplets appear on a part of the railing the finger has just wiped; or the whole railing clears at the drag; or droplets appear where the finger has not been.

pc.expect: The cleared line stays clear while the railing stays cold, or beads slowly back in; it does not fill in at a stroke.
pc.fail: The line fills back in at once behind the finger; or the line clears and beads and clears again with nothing touching it; or the line widens on its own after the finger has gone; or the droplets march back into the line as a front.

pc.expect: The water the finger pushes runs downward or gathers as drops that hang under the rail.
pc.fail: The pushed water runs up the railing; or a drop leaves the railing and rises; or the water gathers along the railing's top and stands as a dome; or the pushed water hangs in the air beside the rail.

pc.expect: The droplets behave as water on metal: they merge where the finger sweeps them together and then hang or run, and the railing stays rigid.
pc.fail: The droplets overlap without merging where the finger sweeps them; or the droplets jump about on the railing; or the railing's metal dents where the finger drags; or the water sets as frost on a summer morning.

pc.expect: One railing; it keeps its shape and the finger passes along its surface, not through it.
pc.fail: The finger passes into the railing; or the railing bends; or a second railing appears; or the railing vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The railing's paint away from the line and the surroundings stay the same.
pc.fail: The railing changes colour; or its paint's pattern changes; or the background changes between frames.
